previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a man with a history of COPD, alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was admitted after presenting with shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain, and altered mental status due to alcohol intoxication. He was treated for a COPD exacerbation with steroids, azithromycin, and nebulized bronchodilators, and for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam and supportive vitamins. His condition improved over two days, with stable oxygen levels and resolution of withdrawal symptoms. A head CT showed no acute injury, and a chest X-ray revealed no pneumonia. He was discharged home with a plan to complete his medication course and find a primary care provider, expressing motivation to stop drinking and re-engage with stable housing and employment.
problems: Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, continuous

 CT chest with contrast  was obtained to look for malignancy

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Cough.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___ chest CT and ___ chest radiograph.

FINDINGS:

The heart size is normal.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged
and within normal limits.  Right middle lobe collapse appears worse when
compared to the prior chest radiograph when there was partial collapse, but
appears similar compared to the prior chest CT.  The pulmonary vascularity is
not engorged.  The left lung is clear.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is
detected.  Old bilateral rib fractures are again noted.  Emphysematous changes
are again seen.  

IMPRESSION:

Recurrent right middle lobe collapse.  Correlation with bronchoscopy or
contrast-enhanced chest CT is again recommended for further assessment.

INDICATION:  ___ man with COPD, hypoxia and collapsed right middle
lobe, assess for malignancy.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the chest
following the uneventful administration of 75 cc of Omnipaque contrast medium.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared.

FINDINGS:  The thyroid gland is normal in appearance with symmetric
enhancement.  The aorta, major branches, heart and pericardium are normal
without pericardial effusion.  Minimal coronary vascular calcification is
seen.  The esophagus is normal in appearance.  There is no pathologic
enlargement of mediastinal, axillary or hilar nodes, though scattered
nonenlarged morphologically normal axillary lymph nodes seen bilaterally.

The trachea is patent with secretions obstructing small airways in the lower
lobes bilaterally. Whispy secretions in patent right middle lobe airwasy are
seen along with a thin band of atelectasis. The right middle lobe airways also
demonstrate bronchial wall thickening suggesting a degree of chronicity. No
obstructing pulmonary mass is identified.  Moderate-to-severe predominantly
centrilobular emphysema is identified as on previous studies.  Ground glass
and nodular opacities in the bilateral bases are also consistent with acute on
chronic aspiration. 

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no lytic or sclerotic bony process concerning
for osseous malignancy.

IMPRESSION: Band of atelectasis in the right middle lobe with right middle
lobe bronchial wall thickening, bilateral lower lobar endobronchial
secretions, and bilateral basilar ground-glass nodularity and opacity
consistent with acute on chronic aspiration.  

No obstructing mass identified.
